gaps.message: Printed part: question 5 (MCQ stem and options A-D), which asks which load-extension graph shows that the load is proportional to the extension for a spring; the official mark scheme keys Q5 = A for 1 mark. The assessed statement is the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 1.5.1 Core item 2 "Sketch, plot and interpret load-extension graphs for an elastic solid and describe the associated experimental procedures." (syllabus sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 12; full-reconciliation/batch-061/official-bullet-evidence.json exact_core_bullet_exception, official_code 1.5.1, core_bullet_number 2). The owning pinned details are forces.resultant-friction with applicability ["core"], recorded in that authority as the "wrong detail for spring extension", and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion with applicability ["supplement"], recorded there as the "wrong tier for this Core question". The frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/13, so calibration_final._validate_selection refuses the supplement detail and no same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent for the load-extension proportionality statement. The Core sibling forces.resultant-friction is retained only as a non-mastery placeholder. Disposition recorded by the authority: blocked_no_exact_core_detail. No label was force-mapped and nothing was promoted.

gaps.message: Printed Core Question 8 (0625/12, whole printed multiple-choice item) requires the mechanical working equation W = F x d, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.7.2 item 2 "Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = ∆E". Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is work.mechanical-equation, recorded on disk with detail_applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.7.2), while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/12, so calibration_final._validate_selection rejects the selection ("Core paper cannot select Supplement detail"). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2, core-column body x0 = 62.4) where item 2 "Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = ∆E" is printed in the Core column and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all; the column evidence file data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json records verdict printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement for work.mechanical-equation and the ledger data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json records the confirmed contradiction. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: work.energy-transfer owns printed Core 1.7.2 item 1 "Understand that mechanical or electrical work done is equal to the energy transferred" but does not state the force x distance equation the marking requires, so it is retained only as the sibling Core owner under official code 1.7.2 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This is an MCQ-shaped blocked row of the known W = Fd class; no Core label was forced and nothing was promoted.

Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ['supplement'] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2, Core-column body line_x0 = 62.4) where item 2 is printed in the Core column and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all; data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json records printed_column 'core' with verdict_vs_pinned printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement for work.mechanical-equation and data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json records the confirmed contradicting print. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: work.energy-transfer owns printed Core 1.7.2 item 1 'Understand that mechanical or electrical work done is equal to the energy transferred' but does not state the force x distance equation the marking requires, so it is retained only as the sibling Core owner under official code 1.7.2 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. gaps.message: Printed part: question 17 (MCQ stem and rows 1-2). The marked statement is the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 2.2.1 Supplement item 3 "Explain, in terms of the motion and arrangement of particles, the relative order of magnitudes of the expansion of solids, liquids and gases as their temperatures rise" (syllabus sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF p.20 / printed p.18, Supplement column x0=309.0/326.0), whose owning pinned detail thermal-expansion.particle-account carries applicability ["supplement"]. The frozen Core paper 0625/12 assesses this particle-level relative-order statement, but no Core-applicability detail under official code 2.2.1 is source-equivalent: thermal-expansion.applications owns only the printed Core items 1 and 2 (the qualitative thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases and its everyday applications and consequences), which state neither the relative order of magnitudes nor the comparison of the average separation of the molecules. The row is therefore blocked, not force-labelled; the retained Core tuple is a provisional primary only, not semantic approval.
gaps.official_bullet: 0625 syllabus 2023-2025, 2.2.1 Thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, Supplement item 3 (PDF p.20 / printed p.18): "Explain, in terms of the motion and arrangement of particles, the relative order of magnitudes of the expansion of solids, liquids and gases as their temperatures rise". The Core column of 2.2.1 carries items 1 and 2 (qualitative thermal expansion at constant pressure; everyday applications and consequences) at x0=62.4/79.4.
gaps.why_no_same_tier_detail: The pinned applicability for thermal-expansion.particle-account is ["supplement"] and print agrees (the relative-order statement is printed in the Supplement column at x0=326.0), so taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects it on the frozen Core paper 0625/12 ("paper tier: Core paper cannot select Supplement detail"). The only Core-applicability detail under official code 2.2.1 is thermal-expansion.applications, whose printed bullets are Core items 1 and 2 and do not state the relative order of magnitudes of expansion or the comparison of the average separation of the molecules, so it is not source-equivalent. Recorded with both values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] and the printed Supplement column at x0=309.0/326.0 agree, and no same-tier Core detail owns the assessed statement.

The only owning detail for that bullet in the pinned overlay is wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction with on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], although the printed column for that bullet is Core, so the equation is not selectable on this Core paper; the on-disk Core-pinned sibling wave-properties.energy-and-features ["core"] covers only Core items 1-3 (waves transfer energy without transferring matter, wave motion as vibrations in ropes, springs and water waves, and the features of a wave) and does not state v = f λ, so no same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent for the materially assessed part.

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q18 stem and options A–D). The marked operation is the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 3.1 item 4 'Recall and use the equation for wave speed v = f λ' (frequency = 4.0 waves / 10 s = 0.40 Hz, wavelength = 2.0 / 0.40 = 5.0 m; printed answer-key row 18 = C). Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 3.1), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/11 the validator refuses that detail (Core paper cannot select Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 22 / printed page 20, section 3.1 item 4) 'Recall and use the equation for wave speed v = f λ' printed in the Core column (only the quantitative wavelength/gap-size dependence is Supplement, items 9 and 10). No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: wave-properties.energy-and-features owns the printed Core statements on energy transfer (item 1), wave features (item 3), transverse/longitudinal modelling (items 5 and 6) and the wave behaviours (items 7 and 8) but does not express the v = f λ equation the marking requires, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 3.1 and is not promoted to the assessed statement. Recorded as a taxonomy_applicability_gap, never force-labelled; this detail is the confirmed printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement case in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json.

gaps.message: Printed mark scheme keys Q18 = B for 1 mark, and the printed item requires diffraction of water waves through a 2.0 cm gap (the wavefronts become semicircular and remain 3.0 cm apart because the water depth and wave speed are unchanged). The exact detail for that operation, wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction, is recorded on disk with detail_applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 3.1) while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/13, so calibration_final._validate_selection rejects the selection. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, printed page 21, section 3.1 Core items 7(c) and 8(c)) "diffraction through a narrow gap" and "diffraction due to a gap" printed in the Core column (only the quantitative wavelength/gap-size dependence is Supplement, 3.1 items 9-10). The Core sibling wave-properties.energy-and-features does not express diffraction and is retained only as a non-mastery placeholder; no label was force-mapped and nothing was promoted.

Its owning pinned detail wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction carries applicability ["supplement"], so the frozen Core paper 0625/12 refuses it and no same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent (wave-properties.energy-and-features owns the printed Core items 1-3 only, the transfer of energy by waves and the features of a wave). The row is therefore blocked, not force-labelled.
gaps.official_bullet: 0625 syllabus 2023-2025, 3.1 General properties of waves, Core item 4 (PDF p.22 / printed p.20): "Recall and use the equation for wave speed v = f lambda". The printed Core column also holds items 1-3, 5-8 (energy transfer by waves, reflection, refraction and diffraction, ripple-tank demonstrations); the 3.1 Supplement column holds items 9 and 10 (the dependence of diffraction on wavelength and gap size).
gaps.why_no_same_tier_detail: The pinned applicability for wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction is ["supplement"], so taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects it on the frozen Core paper 0625/12 ("paper tier: Core paper cannot select Supplement detail"). The only Core-applicability detail under official code 3.1 is wave-properties.energy-and-features, whose printed bullets are Core items 1-3 and do not state the wave-speed equation, so it is not source-equivalent. Recorded with both values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed Core column at x0=62.4/79.4, the confirmed wave-properties.wave-speed-and-diffraction printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement case in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json.

questions.accessibleText: 27 The table gives data for four different electrical devices. Which device develops the greatest power? device voltage current A car headlight 12 V 3.0 A B cooling fan 110 V 0.40 A C electric spark generator 400 kV 0.10 mA D mains lamp 240 V 0.20 A

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q27 stem, the device/voltage/current table and options A–D). The marked operation is selecting the device developing the greatest power from P = I × V (12 V × 3.0 A = 36 W; 110 V × 0.40 A = 44 W; 400 kV × 0.10 mA = 40 W; 240 V × 0.20 A = 48 W; printed answer-key row 27 = D). The printed owning bullet is the 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV', whose owning detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations is stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), so the Core paper 0625/11 cannot select it. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29 / printed page 27, section 4.2.5) where item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV' and item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' are printed in the Core column and the 4.2.5 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy, such as an electrical cell or mains supply, to the circuit components and then into the surroundings' and does not state the P = IV equation, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 4.2.5 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This detail is a confirmed printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement case in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json.

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q31 stem, the series circuit diagram and options A–D). The marked operations are the printed 2023-2025 Core bullets 4.3.2 item 3 'Calculate the combined e.m.f. of several sources in series' (three 1.5 V cells = 4.5 V) and item 4 'Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series' (two 20 Ω resistors = 40 Ω); printed answer-key row 31 = D. Their owning detail in the pinned overlay is series-parallel.combined-values, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.3.2), so the Core paper 0625/11 cannot select it. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 30 / printed page 28, section 4.3.2) where item 3 and item 4 are printed in the Core column and only item 10 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel' is printed in the Supplement column; the detail therefore packages printed Core bullets together with a printed Supplement bullet under one id, which is the structural finding recorded in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: series-parallel.rules-and-lamps owns the Core statements on series current (item 1), constructing and using series and parallel circuits (item 2), the parallel current statement (item 5), the parallel-resistance comparison (item 6) and lamps in parallel (item 7), and does not express the combined e.m.f. or combined series resistance calculations, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 4.3.2 and the marked operations are left unlabelled rather than force-mapped.

Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ['supplement'] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 39 / printed page 37, section 6.1.2 item 3, Core-column body line_x0 = 62.4) where the two 6.1.2 item 3 statements are printed in the Core column; data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json records printed_column 'core' with verdict_vs_pinned printed_spans_both_columns for space-solar-system.orbits-and-gravity (its Supplement column items 7-10 include 6.1.2 item 9) and data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json records the Core item 3 defect. The detail therefore spans both printed columns, so no Core-tier selection of it is lawful on a Core paper; no same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent either: space-solar-system.objects-and-formation is the only Core detail under official code 6.1.2 and owns the Solar-System inventory and formation statements, not the surface-field-strength-versus-planet-mass or field-strength-versus-distance relation, so it is retained only as the sibling Core owner under official code 6.1.2 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This is an MCQ-shaped blocked row of the known 6.1.2 gravitational-field class; no Core label was forced.
gaps.official_bullet: 0625 syllabus 2023-2025, 6.1.2 The Solar System, Core item 3 (PDF page 39 / printed page 37): Know that the strength of the gravitational field (a) at the surface of a planet depends on the mass of the planet (b) around a planet decreases as the distance from the planet increases.

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (printed MCQ Q36 stem and table with the half-life and type-of-radiation-emitted columns, options A-D). The item assesses the printed 2023-2025 Supplement bullet 5.2.4 item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including: ... (b) irradiating food to kill bacteria" (syllabus PDF page 36). The credited row C requires a half-life of several hours and gamma-only emission, i.e. the isotope is selected by its half-life and radiation type for the food-irradiation application. The pinned taxonomy owns only one Supplement detail under mapping 5.2.4, half-life.background-not-subtracted (= Supplement bullet 5.2.4 item 2, calculating half-life from data or decay curves where background radiation has not been subtracted), and no detail at all for the isotope-application bullet 5.2.4 item 3. The printed Core bullets of 5.2.4 are only bullet 1 (define half-life as the time taken for half the nuclei of that isotope in any sample to decay and use it in simple calculations which might involve information in tables or decay curves), recorded as the detail half-life.tables-and-curves, which does not cover choosing a radionuclide for an application; it is the Core owner of subtopic half-life for official code 5.2.4 only, not a source-equivalent label. The nearest candidate labels are not source-equivalent either: nuclear-emissions.fields-and-applications (Supplement, 5.2.2) owns the deflection of the emissions in electric and magnetic fields and the explanation of their relative ionising effects, not isotope selection by half-life and radiation type for an application; nuclear-emissions.nature-ionisation-penetration (Core, 5.2.2) owns the relative ionising and penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma emissions, again not the isotope choice for an application. No Core or Supplement detail in the pinned overlay owns the assessed 5.2.4 item 3(b) food-irradiation isotope-selection operation, so the row stays unresolved rather than forcing a label.

gaps.message: Printed part 11(a) asks the candidate to state why the gravitational field strength at the surface of the Earth is greater than the gravitational field strength at the surface of Mars; the official mark scheme page 13 credits 'Earth has greater mass ORA' B1. The owning printed statement is 2023-2025 Core 6.1.2 item 3 'Know that the strength of the gravitational field (a) at the surface of a planet depends on the mass of the planet (b) around a planet decreases as the distance from the planet increases' (PDF page 39 / printed page 37, Core column x0 = 62.4), but no same-tier Core detail owns it: space-solar-system.orbits-and-gravity (the detail that expresses the planet-field statement, and the only 6.1.2 detail whose Supplement item 8 covers planetary gravitational field strength) is pinned ["supplement"] and cannot be selected on this Core paper (0625/31 is Paper 3 Theory (Core)), while space-solar-system.objects-and-formation (Core) packages only printed Core items 1, 2 and 4 (the Solar System's contents and formation and light-travel time). The part is left unresolved; the row keeps the Core primary space-solar-system.objects-and-formation for the parts that do have a Core owner.

gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(i): "Strontium-90 is used to measure the thickness of metal sheets in industry. ... Suggest why strontium-90 is a suitable radioactive source to measure the thickness of the metal sheets." The official mark scheme credits "(there is a) different count rate with different thicknesses of metal OR number of beta-particles detected varies with thickness" A2 with "(beta (beta) particles) can penetrate thin / 0.75 mm metal OR (beta (beta) particles) are stopped by thick metal" C1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption" (PDF page 36 / printed page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 326.0; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (on-disk detail_applicability ["core"], printed Core item 1 only - the half-life definition and simple calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for a thickness-measuring application: the printed Supplement applications bullet 3(d) has no owning detail, so no detail on any tier carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy, not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Same settled disposition as batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37), batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10) and batch-131 (0625-2025-s-22-q35) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: no owning detail for the printed 5.2.4 item 3 applications bullet (thickness measurement)

gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(ii): "The radiation detector is used to measure the thickness of the aluminium sheets and control the gap between the rollers. State the most suitable radioactive source in Table 9.1 for the machine in Fig. 9.2. Explain why this radioactive source is the most suitable and why the other sources are unsuitable." The official mark scheme credits R (B1); "half-life not too short OR half-life is suitable so that source does not need to be replaced often" (B1); "so count rate changes with thickness" (B1); "gamma-rays would not be stopped at all AND alpha-particles would be absorbed by any thickness of aluminium" (B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption" (PDF page 36 / printed page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 326.0; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (on-disk detail_applicability ["core"], printed Core item 1 only - the half-life definition and simple calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background radiation has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for a thickness-measuring application: the printed Supplement applications bullet 3(d) has no owning detail, so no detail on any tier carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy, not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Same settled disposition as batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37), batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10), batch-124 (0625-2025-m-42-q9) and batch-131 (0625-2025-s-22-q35) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.

gaps.message: Printed parts 1(a)-(e) credit spring / load-extension content: the five stretched-length readings and the best-fit line of l / cm against m / g assess the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 1.5.1 Effects of forces Core item 2 "Sketch, plot and interpret load-extension graphs for an elastic solid and describe the associated experimental procedures" (PDF page 14, Core column, x0 = 79.4; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0), and the Supplement column of the same code (x0 = 326.0) prints the spring-constant statement "Define the spring constant as force per unit extension; recall and use the equation F = kx". On disk the era 2023_2025 official code 1.5.1 owns exactly two details: forces.resultant-friction with detail_applicability ["core"] and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion with detail_applicability ["supplement"]. The Core-printed load-extension statement has no exact Core owner - the repo's own official-bullet evidence (data/classification/full-reconciliation/batch-061/official-bullet-evidence.json) records forces.resultant-friction as the "wrong detail for spring extension" and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion as the "wrong tier", disposition blocked_no_exact_core_detail - and 0625/52 is an all_candidates paper on which a Supplement content selection is rejected, so neither owning detail is selectable at this tier. No nearest label was forced; the row keeps its practical-skill evidence and is left unresolved for a taxonomy-owner decision. Same settled disposition as batch-075 (0625-2023-s-52-q1, 0625-2023-s-62-q1) and batch-105 (0625-2024-s-61-q1, 0625-2024-s-62-q1) for the same spring load-extension practical.

gaps.message: Printed part 2(e)(i) of 0625-2025-w-53-q2 materially assesses COMBINED RESISTANCE and has no tier-legal owner on this all_candidates P5 paper. The question connects one, two and three IDENTICAL resistance wires in parallel (circuits A, B and C, all at l = 95.0 cm) and asks the candidate to record RA, then calculate RB = R x 2 (from circuit B) and RC = R x 3 (from circuit C) and to compare them (2(e)(ii)); MS 2(e)(i) credits 'calculations correct' and 'RA RB and RC within 10% of each other', i.e. the equal-resistor case of the parallel combined-resistance relation, and 2(e)(ii) reasons on the same values. The printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c) places the combined-resistance statements in 4.3.2 Series and parallel circuits on syllabus PDF page 30 (printed page 28): Core item 6 (x0 = 62.4 / 79.4) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' and Supplement item 10 (x0 = 309.0) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'. On disk the era 2023_2025 code 4.3.2 owns exactly two details: series-parallel.rules-and-lamps with detail_applicability ['core'] and series-parallel.combined-values with detail_applicability ['supplement']; only series-parallel.combined-values owns the combined-resistance statements, and it is pinned supplement, so the printed-Core parallel statement has no same-tier owner and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps is not source-equivalent. This is an all_candidates P5 paper, so taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'); no Core-adjacent detail was substituted and the part is not labelled. Same settled disposition and same operation as batch-138 0625-2025-s-53-q3 (parts were also supplied by the question paper there) and batch-139 0625-2025-s-63-q3, and the same blocked class as batch-140 0625-2025-w-11-q28. The remaining marks of the row are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries; the row keeps its practical evidence and is left unresolved for a taxonomy-owner decision.
gaps.official_bullet: 4.3.2 item 6 (Core print) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' / item 10 (Supplement print) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: an era-scoped taxonomy re-seal that gives the printed-Core parallel combined-resistance statement a Core-applicability owner on all_candidates practical papers

gaps.message: Printed part (d)(i) of 0625-2025-s-53-q3 materially assesses COMBINED RESISTANCE and has no tier-legal owner on this Core (all_candidates P5) paper. The question gives two equal resistors: circuit A (R1 in parallel with R2) is worked up with RA = 2R, circuit B (R1 alone) with RB = R from circuit B, and circuit C (R1 in series with R2) with RC = R / 2; MS 3(d)(i) credits 'calculations correct' and 'RA RB and RC within 10% of each other', i.e. the equal-resistor case of the series and parallel combined-resistance relations. The printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c) places those statements in the CORE column of 4.3.2 Series and parallel circuits on syllabus PDF page 30 (printed page 28): Core item 4 (x0 = 79.4) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series' and Core item 6 (x0 = 79.4) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself', while the Supplement column (x0 = 309.0 / 326.0) prints item 10 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'. On disk the era 2023_2025 code 4.3.2 owns exactly two details: series-parallel.rules-and-lamps with detail_applicability ['core'] and series-parallel.combined-values with detail_applicability ['supplement']; only series-parallel.combined-values owns the combined-resistance statements, and it is pinned supplement, so the printed-Core part has no same-tier owner and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations (it is not source-equivalent). This is an all_candidates P5/P6 paper and taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection on such a paper ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'), so the part is not labelable and no Core-adjacent detail was substituted. The remaining printed parts are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries.
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: an era-scoped taxonomy re-seal that gives the printed 2023-2025 Core 4.3.2 combined-resistance statements (items 4 and 6) a Core-applicability owner, e.g. by moving series-parallel.combined-values to ['core'] for era 2023_2025 or by splitting it into a Core series/parallel combined-resistance detail and a Supplement parallel-calculation detail

On disk the era 2023_2025 official code 1.5.1 owns exactly two details: forces.resultant-friction with detail_applicability ["core"] and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion with detail_applicability ["supplement"]. The Core-printed load-extension statement has no exact Core owner - the repo's own official-bullet evidence (data/classification/full-reconciliation/batch-061/official-bullet-evidence.json) records forces.resultant-friction as the "wrong detail for spring extension" and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion as the "wrong tier", disposition blocked_no_exact_core_detail - and 0625/62 is an all_candidates paper on which a Supplement content selection is rejected, so neither owning detail is selectable at this tier. No nearest label was forced; the row keeps its practical-skill evidence and is left unresolved for a taxonomy-owner decision. Same settled disposition as batch-075 (0625-2023-s-62-q1) and batch-105 (0625-2024-s-62-q1) for the same spring load-extension practical.

gaps.message: Printed part 2(d)(i) of 0625-2025-w-63-q2 materially assesses the COMBINED RESISTANCE of identical wires connected in parallel: the student records RA as the value of R from Circuit A (one wire), then calculates RB = R x 2 from the resistance of the two-wire parallel combination in Circuit B and RC = R x 3 from the three-wire parallel combination in Circuit C, i.e. the single-wire resistance is obtained from the parallel-combination resistance. MS 2(d)(i) credits 'RA = 8.06, RB = 7.46 and RC = 7.50 (ohm) OR RA = 8.1, RB = 7.4 OR 7.5 and RC = 7.5 (ohm)'. Official code 4.3.2 (Series and parallel circuits). The owning detail series-parallel.combined-values is stored with applicability ['supplement'] in the pinned overlay, while the printed 2023-2025 syllabus splits the combined-resistance statements across the two columns: 4.3.2 Core item 4 'Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series' and Core item 6 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' are printed in the CORE column (x0 = 62.4 / body x0 = 79.4), and only the parallel calculation Supplement item 10 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel' is printed in the Supplement column (x0 = 309.0 / body x0 = 326.0); the split is recorded verbatim in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json (detail_id series-parallel.combined-values, verdict_vs_pinned printed_spans_both_columns, pdf_page 30, printed_page 28, pinned applicability ['supplement']), and the pinned syllabus sha256 is ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c. This row is a P6 all_candidates (alternative-to-practical) paper, so a Supplement content selection is not lawful - taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects it with 'all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills' - and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations, so substituting it would not be source-equivalent. Recorded as blocked rather than force-labelled, per the batch-134 reconciliation rule and the same-series settled precedents 0625-2025-s-63-q3 (blocked at 3(c)(i)) and 0625-2025-s-53-q3 (blocked at (d)(i)). The remaining marks of the row are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.3.1 / 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries.

This row is a P6 all_candidates (alternative-to-practical) row, so a Supplement content selection is not lawful and the printed statement has no exact same-tier Core owner; the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations, so substituting it would not be source-equivalent. Recorded as blocked rather than force-labelled, per the batch-134 reconciliation rule and the same-paper precedent batch-140 0625-2025-w-11-q28, which blocked the combined resistance of 3.0 ohm and 6.0 ohm in parallel on this paper. The remaining marks of the row are carried by the practical-skills labels (practical.data-recording covers 3(c)(i) as recorded data), and the voltmeter and variable-resistor symbols and the R = V / I calculations carry 4.3.1 and 4.2.4, both pinned Core.

The marked operation is reading the load-extension graph of a steel spring to obtain the load at a given extension (extension 6.0 cm - 2.0 cm = 4.0 cm gives a load of 1.0 N, keyed answer B), which is printed 2023-2025 Core 1.5.1 item 2 'Sketch, plot and interpret load-extension graphs for an elastic solid and describe the associated experimental procedures' (syllabus PDF page 12, Core column). The pinned taxonomy has no Core detail for spring load-extension content: the exact spring detail forces.spring-constant-circular-motion is recorded with detail_applicability ["supplement"] while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core", and the sibling Core detail forces.resultant-friction does not cover spring load-extension content. No exact Core label is available, so the row is not forced; forces.resultant-friction is retained only as the declared source-tuple Core fallback.

gaps.message: The paired QP/MS assess the random (Brownian) movement of smoke particles as caused by collisions with air particles: QP 10 (0625/11 M/J 24) asks "Why do the smoke particles move randomly?" and the printed mark scheme keys answer A "They are hit by air particles". The pinned 2023_2025 taxonomy owns that collision content only in particle-model.forces-and-collisions, whose on-disk detail_applicability is ["supplement"] (official code 2.1.2); this is a core paper (on-disk paper_tier "core", component 11) and calibration_final._validate_selection rejects a Supplement detail on a Core paper ("Core paper cannot select Supplement detail"). No core-applicable detail expresses the collision cause, so the nearest core detail particle-model.arrangement-motion is retained only as a non-mastery placeholder.

Since then, the radiation has shifted to the microwave region of the electromagnetic spectrum. How has this change affected the wavelength and speed of the radiation? wavelength speed A decreased decreased B decreased stayed the same C increased decreased D increased stayed the same

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q22 stem and options A-D). The marked criterion (early-Universe gamma radiation that has shifted into the microwave region, with wavelength increased and speed unchanged) is the printed Supplement-only bullet 6.2.3(6) 'Explain that the CMBR was produced shortly after the Universe was formed and that this radiation has been expanded into the microwave region of the electromagnetic spectrum as the Universe expanded', owned by the Supplement-only detail space-universe.cmb-hubble-and-age. The printed Core bullets of 6.2.3 are 1 (Milky Way is one of many billions of galaxies, diameter approx. 100 000 light-years), 2 (redshift as an increase in the observed wavelength of radiation emitted from receding stars and galaxies), 3 (light from distant galaxies appears redshifted compared with light emitted on the Earth) and 4 (redshift in light from distant galaxies is evidence that the Universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang Theory): none of them covers primordial radiation filling the Universe being stretched by expansion, so no Core detail is source-equivalent and space-universe.milky-way-redshift-big-bang is recorded only as the Core owner of subtopic space-universe for official code 6.2.3, not as a source-equivalent label.

The printed owning bullet is the 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV', whose owning detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations is stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), so the Core paper 0625/12 cannot select it. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29 / printed page 27, section 4.2.5) where item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV' and item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' are printed in the Core column and the 4.2.5 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy, such as an electrical cell or mains supply, to the circuit components and then into the surroundings' and does not state the P = IV equation, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 4.2.5 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped.

gaps.message: Paired QP/MS inspection of 0625/13 Q27 shows the printed item gives a current I in a resistor for a time t with potential difference V and asks what the product IVt represents, and the official mark scheme awards row Q27 answer B – 1 mark, the energy transferred by the resistor. That assessed operation is the electrical energy equation E = IVt, which the frozen 2023_2025 taxonomy exposes only as the Supplement-only detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, and a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail; official code 4.2.5 exposes only electrical-work-power.energy-transfer as Core (understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source to the circuit components and then into the surroundings), which is not equivalent to the E = IVt operation. The pinned official 2023-2025 guide (source official-2023-2025, sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, page 29) prints 'recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' in the Core column of 4.2.5 (word x0 = 79.37), so this is recorded as an unresolved applicability conflict rather than forcing Q27 into the nearby Core label. The retained Core 4.2.5 anchor is not semantic approval of the E = IVt operation.

The item assesses the printed 2023-2025 Supplement bullet 5.2.4(3)(d) 'Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption' - a beta-particle source and detector whose count rate falls as the paper thickness increases, with the rollers squeezing below 12 counts/s and stopping above 13 counts/s. The pinned taxonomy owns only one Supplement detail under mapping 5.2.4, half-life.background-not-subtracted (= Supplement bullet 5.2.4(2), calculating half-life from data where background has not been subtracted), and no detail at all for the isotope-application bullet 5.2.4(3)(d). The printed Core bullets of 5.2.4 are only bullet 1 (define half-life as the time taken for half the nuclei in any sample to decay and use it in simple calculations from tables or decay curves), which does not cover choosing a radionuclide for a thickness gauge; half-life.tables-and-curves is recorded only as the Core owner of subtopic half-life for official code 5.2.4, not as a source-equivalent label. The candidate nearest labels are not source-equivalent either: nuclear-emissions.nature-ionisation-penetration (Core, 5.2.2) owns the relative ionising and penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma emissions, not an absorption-based thickness-control application, and nuclear-emissions.fields-and-applications (Supplement, 5.2.2) owns deflection of the emissions in electric/magnetic fields and the explanation of their relative ionising effects, not isotope selection for measuring and controlling material thickness. No Core or Supplement detail in the pinned overlay owns the assessed thickness-control application, so the row stays unresolved rather than forcing a label.

gaps.message: Printed part: (b)(ii). The marked operation is the mechanical working equation, work done = force x distance (the cyclist exerts 36 N over 250 m; the official mark scheme credits '9000' A3, '36 x 250' (C2), '(work =) force x distance in any form' (C1) and 'J' B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.7.2 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = dE'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is work.mechanical-equation (era 2023_2025, official code 1.7.2), stored with applicability ["supplement"], and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/33 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17), whose 1.7.2 Supplement column is empty and lists W = Fd = dE as Core item 2; the Core owner work.energy-transfer covers only the work-equals-energy-transferred bullet, not the equation, so no Core detail is source-equivalent and the part is not legally labelable on the pinned taxonomy. Marked unresolved rather than forcing a nearest Core label.

gaps.message: Printed part: (b)(i) and (b)(ii). The marked operation is reading a load-extension graph for a spring and combining the extension with the printed natural length (the official mark scheme credits '1.6 (cm)' A2 and 'any indication of correct attempt on graph' C1 for (b)(i), and '9.6 (cm)' B1 for (b)(ii)), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.5.1 item 2 'Sketch, plot and interpret load-extension graphs for an elastic solid and describe the associated experimental procedures'. The pinned overlay owns the whole 1.5.1 subtopic with only two details and neither is source-equivalent at the required tier: forces.resultant-friction is applicability ["core"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.5.1) but does not own the load-extension/spring-extension statement, and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion is applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.5.1), which the validator refuses on this Core paper (0625/33 is Paper 3 Theory (Core)). Applicability/source defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["core" for forces.resultant-friction, "supplement" for forces.spring-constant-circular-motion] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 14 / printed page 12, section 1.5.1) where item 2 'Sketch, plot and interpret load-extension graphs for an elastic solid and describe the associated experimental procedures' is printed in the Core column. This is the exact_core_bullet_exception case 0625-2023-m-12-q9 recorded with disposition blocked_no_exact_core_detail (reconciliation 2023_2025 authority data/classification/full-reconciliation/batch-061/official-bullet-evidence.json, which rules forces.resultant-friction the wrong detail for spring extension and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion the wrong tier for this Core question); no Core detail is source-equivalent, so the spring parts are left unlabelled rather than force-mapped.

The marked operation is the mechanical working equation, work done = force x distance (the car of weight 14 000 N is lifted vertically 0.78 m onto the recovery vehicle; the official mark scheme credits '11 000' A3, '14 000 x 0.78' C2, '(work =) force x distance OR (W =) F x d' C1 and 'J' B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.7.2 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = dE'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is work.mechanical-equation, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.7.2), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2) where item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = dE' is printed in the Core column and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: work.energy-transfer owns printed Core 1.7.2 item 1 'Understand that mechanical or electrical work done is equal to the energy transferred' but does not state the force x distance equation the marking credits, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 1.7.2 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This is the work.mechanical-equation printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement case recorded in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json.

gaps.message: Printed part: (b)(ii). The marked operation is the electrical energy equation E = IVt (the 0.20 A current through the lamp at 5.4 V for 30 s; the official mark scheme credits '32 (J)' A3, '(E =) 5.4 x 0.2 x 30' C2 and '(E =) VIt OR P x t OR I2 x R x t' C1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect checked against the pinned official syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29 / printed page 27, section 4.2.5) where items 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV' and 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' are printed in the Core column. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy ... to the circuit components and then into the surroundings' but does not state the E = IVt equation the marking credits, so the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This is the electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations defect recorded in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json.

gaps.message: Printed Core part 9(b)(ii) requires the electrical power equation P = IV (official mark scheme: '(P =) 320 (W)' A3 from '(P =) 1.4 x 230', with '(P =) I x V' C1). The exact 2023_2025 detail for that equation, electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, is recorded on disk with detail_applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5) while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/31, so calibration_final._validate_selection rejects the selection. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, printed page 27 / PDF page 29, section 4.2.5 items 2 and 3) "Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV" and "Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt" printed in the Core column (4.2.5 carries no Supplement items). The same-statement Core sibling electrical-work-power.energy-transfer does not express the quantitative power relation the marking requires, so it is not source-equivalent; the retained Core anchor transformer.construction-and-transmission (part (b)(i), 3 marks) is a non-mastery placeholder. The same power relation was blocked for the same reason in batch-128 q31 and batch-085 (0625-2023-w-31-q6, 0625-2023-w-32-q9). No Core label was force-mapped and this element stays unresolved.

gaps.message: Printed part (b)(ii) 'Calculate the energy transferred electrically when the current calculated in (b)(i) is present in resistor Q for 5 minutes' is credited by MS 6(b)(ii) '610 J  OR  620 J' A3 with 'E = I × V × t  OR  (E =) V × I × t  OR  (E =) 12 × 0.17 × 300' C1 and '300 (s) OR 5 × 60' C1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' (syllabus PDF p.29, printed page 27, Core column x=62.4, next to Core item 2 'P = IV'). The owning pinned detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations carries applicability ['supplement'] only, so the Core-printed statement has no same-tier owning detail: labelling it 'supplement' would misstate the printed column and no source-equivalent Core detail exists. The only Core-applicability detail under 4.2.5 is electrical-work-power.energy-transfer, whose printed bullet is item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy, such as an electrical cell or mains supply, to the circuit components and then into the surroundings', not the electrical energy equation. The nearest equation detail elsewhere is 1.7.2 work.mechanical-equation, which owns the mechanical equation W = Fd = ΔE (and is itself printed Core but pinned Supplement), so it is not source-equivalent for E = IVt. The row therefore stays unresolved for this part rather than forcing a nearest label onto a Core-printed statement.

gaps.message: Printed part (a)(iii) requires the corrected count rate (measured count rate 382 counts/min minus the background 26 counts/min = 356 counts/min), the 2023-2025 Supplement statement 5.2.1 item 5. The pinned overlay's 5.2.1 mapping owns only the Core-applicable detail radioactivity-detection.background-and-detectors (detail_applicability ['core']), which expresses the Core statements 1-4 (background radiation, sources, detectors, count rate) and no statement about a corrected count rate, so no owned detail legally expresses this assessed Supplement-band operation. No nearest label is forced.
gaps.printed_bullet: Supplement statement 5.2.1 item 5: 'Use measurements of background radiation to determine a corrected count rate' (syllabus PDF page 35, Supplement column, word x0 = 326.0).

gaps.message: Printed parts (c)(i) and (c)(ii) require an explanation of why the tracer isotope must not have a very short half-life (activity would fall too low for detection) and must not have a very long half-life (contamination of the water supply), i.e. how the half-life determines the suitability of an isotope for this application: the 2023-2025 Supplement statement 5.2.4 item 3. The pinned overlay's 5.2.4 mapping owns only half-life.tables-and-curves (core, definition and simple calculations from tables/curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (supplement, calculating half-life where background radiation has not been subtracted); neither expresses the choice-of-isotope application statement, so no owned detail legally expresses these assessed parts. No nearest label is forced.

gaps.message: Printed part 10(c): "Suggest a use of a radioactive isotope with a half-life of one hour. Explain why a short half-life is suitable for this use." The official mark scheme credits "medical tracers OR medical imaging OR medical diagnosis" - B1 and "any one from: keep dose low / does not stay in body too long / less damage (to body)" - B1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (e) diagnosis and treatment of cancer using gamma rays" (printed page 36 PDF / page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (pinned applicability core, printed Core item 1 only - the definition and simple half-life calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (pinned applicability supplement, printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for an application by its half-life: the pinned Supplement detail names the background-subtraction operation, not the applications bullet, so no same-tier detail carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy (the applications bullet has no detail), not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced.

This is a P5 all_candidates paper and taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection on an all_candidates paper ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'), so the owning detail cannot be selected at this tier. No same-tier detail is source-equivalent: the Core detail refraction.experiment-and-total-internal-reflection rests only on the printed Core items 1-5 of 3.2.2 ('Define and use the terms normal, angle of incidence and angle of refraction'; 'Describe an experiment to show refraction of light by transparent blocks of different shapes'; 'Describe the passage of light through a transparent material'; 'State the meaning of critical angle'; 'Describe internal reflection and total internal reflection'), none of which prints the refractive index, its definition or any equation for n. No nearest Core label was forced; part (c) is left unresolved and unlabelled for a taxonomy-owner decision.

On disk the era 2023_2025 code 1.5.1 owns exactly two details: forces.resultant-friction with detail_applicability ["core"] and forces.spring-constant-circular-motion with detail_applicability ["supplement"]. gaps.message: Printed part (e) is credited by MS 2(e) 'as the current decreases V_LED decreases (or reverse)' and 'and R_LED increases (or reverse)', i.e. the LED (diode) resistance behaviour. Both owning details are pinned ['supplement'] and both printed statements sit in the SUPPLEMENT column: (i) resistance.characteristics-and-proportionality under official code 4.2.4, printed Supplement item 4 'Sketch and explain the current-voltage graphs for a resistor of constant resistance, a filament lamp and a diode' (syllabus SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF p.29 / printed p.27, x0=326.0); and (ii) circuit-diagrams.diode under official code 4.3.1, printed Supplement item 2 'Draw and interpret circuit diagrams containing diodes and light-emitting diodes (LEDs), and know how these components behave in the circuit' (PDF p.30 / printed p.28, x0=326.0). This is a P6 all_candidates paper and taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection on an all_candidates paper, so neither owning detail can be selected at this tier. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: the printed Core items of 4.2.4 are only 'Recall and use the equation for resistance R = V / I', 'Describe an experiment to determine resistance using a voltmeter and an ammeter and do the appropriate calculations' and 'State, qualitatively, the relationship of the resistance of a metallic wire to its length and to its cross-sectional area'; Core 4.3.1 item 1 lists diode-free components; the LED is not a metallic wire, so the diode current-voltage characteristic is not owned by any Core detail. No nearest Core label was forced; part (e) is left unresolved and unlabelled for a taxonomy-owner decision.

gaps.message: Printed Core parts 9(a)(ii) and 9(b) require the electrical power/energy-unit relations I = P / V (720 / 230 = 3.1 A) and the kWh cost calculation (26 kW h x 18 cents = 468 cents). The exact 2023_2025 detail for those operations, electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, is recorded on disk with detail_applicability ["supplement"], while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 and the printed official 2023_2025 syllabus prints the P = IV, E = IVt and kW h cost statements in the Core column of 4.2.5, so calibration_final._validate_selection rejects the selection. The retained Core electrical-work-power.energy-transfer and electrical-safety anchors are non-mastery placeholders; no label was force-mapped and this row remains unresolved.

gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(iii): "The isotope of neptunium produced by americium-241 is also radioactive. ... The half-life of neptunium is longer than two million years. Using this information, explain the advantage of this long half-life for the use and safe disposal of a household smoke alarm." The official mark scheme credits "low(er) (initial) activity OR few emissions per unit time" (M1) "so smoke detectors are not hazardous to humans OR so disposal of old detectors is cheap / easy" (A1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including (a) household fire (smoke) alarms" (printed page 36 PDF / page 34 footer, Supplement column). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (pinned applicability core, printed Core item 1 - the definition and simple half-life calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (pinned applicability supplement, printed Supplement item 2 - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to justifying a radionuclide for an application by its half-life: the pinned Supplement detail names the background-subtraction operation, not the applications bullet, so no same-tier detail carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy (the applications bullet has no detail), not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Recorded identically to the settled practice of batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37) and batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.
